description_html:
In a maximum independent set (MIS) problem, an undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) is given. The goal is to select the largest subset of nodes such that no two selected nodes are connected by an edge in \(G\).

The easy and medium levels are generated with the generator of [Gasse19] on Barabási-Albert graphs with affinity \(m_{BA}=4\) (each new node attaches to 4 existing nodes, so \(|E|=4(|V|-4)\)). This generator does not write one constraint per edge: it first computes a greedy clique partition of \(V\) and replaces the edges inside each clique by a single clique inequality; all remaining edges keep an edge inequality. The very hard levels of [Huang23] are generated on Erdős-Rényi graphs \(G(|V|,p)\) with \(p=8/(|V|-1)\) (expected average degree 8, i.e. about \(4|V|\) edges) and use one edge inequality per edge. All instances are unweighted.

Notation.

  • \(G=(V,E)\): undirected graph; \(x_v\in\{0,1\}\): 1 if node \(v\in V\) is in the independent set.
  • \(\mathcal{Q}\): a collection of cliques of \(G\) (each with at least 2 nodes) such that every edge of \(E\) is contained in exactly one \(Q\in\mathcal{Q}\). For the easy and medium levels, \(\mathcal{Q}\) consists of the cliques of size at least 2 of the greedy clique partition plus every edge not inside one of these cliques; for the very hard levels, \(\mathcal{Q}=E\) (every edge is its own 2-clique).

Formulation.

\begin{align} \max\ & \sum_{v\in V} x_v \\ \textrm{s.t.}\ & \sum_{v\in Q} x_v \leq 1, && \forall Q\in\mathcal{Q}, \\ & x_v\in\{0,1\}, && \forall v\in V. \end{align}

With \(\mathcal{Q}=E\) this is the edge formulation \(x_u+x_v\le 1,\ \forall (u,v)\in E\). Since each edge lies in exactly one \(Q\in\mathcal{Q}\), both forms have the same feasible integer solutions; the clique form has slightly fewer rows (e.g. about 3,950 instead of 3,984 for 1,000 nodes) and a tighter LP relaxation.
changes: Formulation generalized to clique inequalities over an edge-clique partition Q: easy/medium instances (learn2branch generate_indset) use greedy clique-partition rows, very hard instances use plain edge rows.

'Node Degree' column replaced by 'Graph Parameter' (BA affinity m=4; ER edge probability p=8/(n-1), generator parameter edge=4 with p = 2*edge/(n-1)) and 'Avg. Degree' (2|E|/|V|): the old value '4' was the BA affinity for BA levels and the generator's 'edge' argument (half the expected degree) for ER levels, not a node degree.
Fixed typo 'in given' -> 'is given'; noted that all instances are unweighted.
Huang23 text says ER 'average degree 5'; the instances (and Huang23 Table 1 constraint counts 23,977 / 48,027) correspond to about 4|V| edges, i.e. average degree 8. The table follows the instances.
verification: MIS/easy test 0,1: 1000 binaries, 3951 / 3945 rows '<= 1', unit coefficients and objective. Pairs implied by rows = 3984 = 4*(1000-4) BA edges, each edge in exactly one row, min degree 4 (consistent with learn2branch's star-initialized BA). Row sizes: 3938 edges + 12 triangles + 1 5-clique (3984 - 12*2 - 9 = 3951).
MIS/medium test 0,1: 1500 binaries, 5946 / 5938 rows; implied edges 5984 = 4*(1500-4); row sizes 2-4.

MIS/very-hard test 0,1 (MPS from SCIP): 6000 binaries, 24,225 / 23,956 rows, all of length 2 (pure edge rows), no edge repeated, degree 0..22 with 2 isolated nodes, avg degree 8.08 / 7.99, consistent with ER p=8/5999 (expected 23,996 edges; table avg 23,994.82).

Generators: learn2branch 01_generate_instances.py (Graph.barabasi_albert(n, affinity=4), generate_indset with greedy_clique_partition; 1000 and 1500 are its transfer sizes). Very hard: local generator_MVC_MIS_CA_SC_MK.py gen_graph('erdos_renyi', edge=4) -> nx.erdos_renyi_graph(n, p=edge*2/(n-1)), createOptINDSET (edge rows, unit objective); facebookresearch/CL-LNS ships instances named INDSET_ER_6000/instance_ER4_*.cip, matching this naming.
Very hard 2 (12,000 nodes) not on HF: table avg 48,009.62 rows = about 4n, consistent with the same p = 8/(n-1).
open_questions: learn2branch also adds singleton rows x_v <= 1 for any of nodes 0-9 that appear in no constraint; this never happens for BA graphs (min degree 4) and none were found, so the formulation omits it.
